name: Amendments by the committee responsible – put to the vote collectively
title: REPORT on the proposal for a regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council on the Union Civil Protection Mechanism and Union support for health emergency preparedness and response, and repealing Decision No 1313/2013/EU (Union Civil Protection Mechanism)

part_text: Having regard to the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, and in particular Articles 168(5), 196, 322(1), point (a), and 349 thereof, / Having regard to Article 11 of the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, / (1) In view of the significant increase in the numbers, severity and complexity of natural and human-induced hazards in recent years, the strengthening of cooperation in the field of civil protection at Union level is necessary to create a resilient Union with the capacities and the capabilities required to anticipate, manage and respond effectively to those risks and threats, independently of their nature of origin, to ensure that the citizens of the Union enjoy adequate protection. The Union Civil Protection Mechanism (the ‘Union Mechanism’) should fulfil this role by strengthening cooperation and coordination among Member States to enhance the overall ability to prevent, prepare for, and respond to disasters and crises, notably through sustained investment in research and innovation, while promoting a proactive and forward-looking approach to resilience that reduces vulnerabilities and supporting sustainable recovery and reconstruction. The strengthening of interinstitutional cooperation at Union level shall be based on a multi-level governance approach ensuring the full involvement of regional and local authorities, which act as first responders in disaster prevention, preparedness and response. / (1a) In a global context hallmarked by the intensification of natural disasters, technological risks, health crises and the cross-border impact of climate change, as well as recent geo-political developments, there is a pressing need for a better-prepared, more resilient and more cohesive Union. Union action under this Regulation should respect the primary responsibility of Member States for civil protection and disaster management. It should focus on coordination, interoperability and support, particularly in cross-border or major crises, without creating unnecessary duplication of structures; ensuring that Members States and their subnational authorities continue to enjoy the requisite flexibility to adjust the implementation to their own specific contexts. / (3) While prevention and preparedness measures are essential to enhance the resilience of the Union in facing natural and human-induced disasters, the occurrence, timing and magnitude of disasters are by nature unpredictable. Financial resources required to ensure an adequate response can vary significantly from year to year and should be made available immediately. Reconciling the budgetary principle of predictability with the necessity to react rapidly to new needs therefore means having to adapt the financial implementation of the work programmes. Consequently, it is appropriate to authorise carry-over of unused appropriations, limited to the following year and solely devoted to response actions, in addition to the carry-over of appropriations authorised under Article 12(4) of Regulation (EU, Euratom) 2024/2509. Given the urgent and unpredictable nature of the crises, the Union Mechanism should not be encumbered by excessive administrative burdens or procedural constraints, in order to ensure a rapid, efficient and coordinated response in support of the Member States and their regions. This flexibility should also allow for the rapid mobilisation of financial support to regional and local authorities directly affected by disasters. / (4) In a rapidly changing economic, social and geopolitical environment, recent experience has shown the need for a more flexible multiannual financial framework and Union spending programmes. To that effect, the funding should duly consider the evolving policy needs and Union’s priorities as identified in relevant documents published by the Commission, in Council conclusions and European Parliament resolutions, while ensuring sufficient predictability for the budget implementation, which will enable a proper calibration of prevention, preparedness and response priorities. Financial predictability is also crucial in order to ensure a fair and sustainable allocation of resources, enabling Member States to continue investing in strategic capacities and building up reserves of essential goods. / (6) The protection to be ensured under the Union Mechanism should cover people, the environment and biodiversity, property, including housing, critical infrastructure and the operators of essential services as defined in Directive (EU) 2022/2557 of the European Parliament and of the Council1, such as energy and transport by land, air or sea or space infrastructure, and cultural heritage, against all kinds of natural and human-induced disasters. Reference to natural and human-induced disasters should be understood as referring to the consequences of all natural and human-induced hazards. This should include acts of terrorism along with the consequences of armed conflicts on civilian population, technological, radiological or environmental disasters, climate change, marine and inland water pollution, water supply disruptions and water resilience, hydrogeological instability, health emergencies, cross-border health threats, serious supply-chain disruptions, including to energy and food supply chains and other undefined hybrid disasters or emergencies, occurring inside or outside the Union. Some of these disasters may require cross-sectoral coordination in situations where other Union crisis management mechanisms are also applied. This Regulation therefore needs to support strategic reserve management, supply chain diversification and the deployment of critical capacity in crisis situations in the Union, in order to enhance the Union's food security and strategic autonomy. \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ 1 Directive (EU) 2022/2557 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 14 December 2022 on the resilience of critical entities and repealing Council Directive 2008/114/EC (OJ L 333, 27.12.2022, p. 164, ELI: [http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2022/2557/oj](http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2022/2557/oj)). / (7a) This Regulation should promote the raising of public awareness as regards existing risks, prevention measures and appropriate behaviour in emergency situations, including through coordinated information, education, training and communication actions at Union, Member State and regional level. This Regulation should also help to build citizens’ confidence in the Union’s ability to respond effectively to crises by ensuring the visibility of the support provided and by demonstrating through concrete actions the Union’s presence and solidarity in emergency situations, thus helping to strengthen legitimacy and public trust. / (8) To promote consistency in its international action in the field of civil protection, the Union should recognise the key role of intergovernmental organisations through strengthening policy dialogue, exchange of knowledge and best practices as disasters and crises are increasing in scale and scope globally and the risks and threats thereof are shared by the Union. The exchange of knowledge should also include local and regional governance practices and cross-border operational arrangements. / (9a) Disaster risk prevention and management require coherent coordination across all levels of public authority, particularly with regional and local authorities, alongside meaningful engagement with local communities, volunteers, academics, non-governmental organisations, and community-based organisations, taking into account the territorial diversity of the Union and the spatial distribution of vulnerabilities. Given that risks are often cross-border in nature, these assessments need to systematically integrate the sub-national dimension and cooperation between neighbouring regions, to ensure more effective planning and preparedness. In this context, regional and local authorities often bear the frontline responsibility; they assure the direct protection of citizens, manage the immediate impact of crises at local level and coordinate the initial intervention measures. In this framework, investment in locally led resilience structures is a necessary complement to top-down risk management frameworks and helps ensure that preparedness measures are effective, durable, inclusive, and responsive to the specific needs of people and affected communities. The Union Mechanism should formally recognise the role of subnational levels of governance, including regions, municipalities, and cross-border cooperation entities as essential actors across all stages of the disaster management cycle, and ensure that Union support reaches those levels effectively. / 9a. The Knowledge Network shall also promote the active involvement of young people, including through youth organisations and educational institutions. / 3a. Where clear evidence is available from relevant meteorological services in advance of an extraordinary weather event, Member States may trigger the Union Mechanism in a four day period leading up to the weather event to allow equipment such as mobile electricity generators and key equipment of this nature to be transported into the Member State in question and placed in a local area adjacent to the weather event so as to facilitate early usage. / 4. Member States may, subject to appropriate security safeguards, provide information about relevant military response capacities that could be used as last resort as the assistance through the Union Mechanism, such as transport and logistical or medical support. / 8a. Preparedness actions shall demonstrate the operational importance of locally and regionally embedded command structures, with territorial knowledge and rapid decision-making capacity at regional and local level. / 1. The European Civil Protection Pool (ECPP) shall represent the frontline response capacity of the Union Mechanism and shall be a key tool for strengthening Member States' capacity to respond efficiently and effectively to disasters and crises. The ECPP shall be the primary instrument of the Union mechanism. The ECPP shall consist of a pool of voluntarily committed response capacities of the Member States and include modules, other response capacities, categories of experts and technical assistance and support teams (TAST). The Commission shall lay down rules for the identification of Member States experts, modules and other response capacities as well as operational requirements for the functioning and interoperability of modules and deployment in an implementing act adopted in accordance with the examination procedure referred to in Article 35(2). / 2. The assistance provided by a Member State through the ECPP shall be complementary to existing capacities in the requesting Member State, without prejudice to the primary responsibility of Member States for disaster prevention, preparedness, and response on their territory. / 3. On the basis of identified risks and any existing scenario-building as referred to in point (b) of Article 16(1), in cooperation with the Member States, the Commission shall, by means of implementing acts, define the types and specify the number of key response capacities required for the ECPP (‘response capacity goals’). Those implementing acts shall be adopted in accordance with the examination procedure referred to in Article 35(2). / 6. Member States shall on a voluntary basis identify, commit and register the response capacities which they offer to the ECPP, including relevant military capacities that could be used as part of civil protection assistance. The registration of multinational modules provided by two or more Member States shall be undertaken jointly by all the Member States concerned. Member States and regions are encouraged to establish cross-border civil protection arrangements and joint operational units in border regions exposed to shared risks. / 11. Where rescEU capacities consist of equipment or consumable goods, Member States in consultation with the Commission, through the ERCC, may decide to either donate or loan the offered rescEU capacities. / 3a. Pursuant to Article 20 of the Treaty on European Union and Article 196 TFEU , and in accordance with Articles 326 to 334 TFEU, an enhanced cooperation in the field of civil protection shall be established in order to develop deeper operational integration, permanent multinational capacities and harmonised preparedness structures within the framework of this Regulation. This shall further lead to the establishment of permanent rescEU personnel corps that can be put at use immediately once emergency arises across the Union. / 2. The Commission shall, by means of implementing acts, define the response capacities that rescEU shall consist of, based on Union risk assessments in accordance with Article 16(1) taking into account identified and emerging risks and threats, including climate-related and health-related risks and disaster scenarios, the overall response capacities available at Union level, and any capacity gaps identified. The rescEU capacities defined pursuant to this paragraph may include, inter alia: (a) rescEU warehouses; (b) rapidly deployable emergency communication systems to ensure a minimum level of operational communication among all relevant actors where standard communication infrastructure is unavailable or disrupted; (c) capacities aimed at strengthening long-term resilience. Multi-purpose rescEU capacities shall be considered wherever possible. The Commission may support acquisition, lease-to-own and construction of state-owned rescEU warehouses to securely host and develop rescEU capacities, ensuring permanent access to those capacities. Those implementing acts shall be adopted in accordance with the examination procedure referred to in Article 35(2). / 3. rescEU capacities shall be acquired, rented, leased, otherwise contracted by or donated to the Member States, provided that such capacities are based on identified needs. / 6. rescEU capacities shall be hosted by the Member States or the Commission. The Commission and the Member States shall, as appropriate, ensure an adequate geographical distribution of rescEU capacities based on Union risk assessments in accordance with Article 16(1) and taking into account identified and emerging risks and threats. / 7. The Commission shall define quality requirements, by means of implementing acts, for the response capacities forming part of rescEU, in consultation with the Member States. Those implementing acts shall be adopted in accordance with the advisory procedure referred to in Article 35(2). / 7a. The quality requirements shall be based on established international standards, including sustainability standards, where such standards already exist and shall take into account the Union’s goal of strategic autonomy. In this regard, new aerial capacities acquired or financed under rescEU for the purposes of firefighting and the transport of emergency responders, or other aerial emergency response operations, shall be, where available, certified in accordance with Union law and aviation safety requirements and full civil certification from the European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA), enabled by the voluntary opt-in mechanism provided for in Article 2(6) of Regulation 2018/1139 of the European Parliament and of the Council1a. This requirement shall not affect capacities already acquired by the Union and Member States. \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ 1a Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 4 July 2018 on common rules in the field of civil aviation and establishing a European Union Aviation Safety Agency, and amending Regulations (EC) No 2111/2005, (EC) No 1008/2008, (EU) No 996/2010, (EU) No 376/2014 and Directives 2014/30/EU and 2014/53/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council, and repealing Regulations (EC) No 552/2004 and (EC) No 216/2008 of the European Parliament and of the Council and Council Regulation (EEC) No 3922/91 (OJ L 212, 22.8.2018, p. 1, ELI: [http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2018/1139/oj](http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2018/1139/oj)). / 9. rescEU capacities shall be used, including for deployment, national use, loaning or donations, and managing rescEU strategic reserves, in accordance with implementing acts adopted in accordance with the examination procedure referred to in Article 35(2). / 3a. Where a Member State decides to issue a public warning to its population about an ongoing or imminent disaster within its territory, which causes or is likely to cause transboundary effects, it shall share this warning without delay with the potentially affected Member States and the Commission. Member States shall ensure that their procedures for issuing public warnings in such situations are sufficiently clear to ensure rapid dissemination and sharing with other Member States and shall include information about this capacity as part of their summary of national risk management information submitted to the Commission in accordance with Article 15. / Article 24a Trusted communication in Disaster Risk Management 1. The Commission shall support Member States in ensuring that their national risk management planning includes a dedicated communication strategy based on the principles of transparency, timeliness, consistency and inclusiveness, with a view to building and maintaining public trust in public warnings and guidance before, during and after a disaster or crisis. 2. The Commission shall, in cooperation with Member States, take into account best practices to develop guidelines for the implementation of the principles set out in this Article. 3. Member States shall take effective measures to prevent, detect and counteract the spread of misinformation and disinformation related to disasters, risks and threats that may undermine the effectiveness of official emergency communication. Those measures shall be taken in accordance with existing Union programmes and instruments. / Article 24b An integrated Union space service for the Public Warning systems EUSPA shall ensure an Integrated Union space service for the Public Warning systems combining the use of the services provided individually by the Union space components, including Positioning, Navigation and Timing (PNT), Earth Observation, Secure Connectivity and Space Situational Awareness, enabling the provision of coherent, sovereign and interoperable space-enabled solutions delivered to meet the civil protection needs. These services shall be delivered through interoperable user interfaces, service platforms and terminals, enabling seamless access to Union space capabilities within the crisis and disaster risk management cycles. This requirement shall not imply funding for the EUSPA under this Regulation, which is addressed in other Union instruments. / 4. The ERCC shall have access to operational, analytical, monitoring, information management and communication capabilities, and shall be equipped with all resources needed in terms of personnel and tools necessary to receive and process EU classified information, to address a broad range of disasters and emergencies within and outside the Union. The processing of classified information and security-sensitive data by the ERCC shall be carried out in accordance with the applicable Union rules, in particular Council Decision 2013/488/EU and Commission Decision (EU, Euratom) 2015/444, and subject to the express consent of the transmitting Member State in accordance with the originator control principle. / 4a. The ERCC shall support interoperability between Union-level digital tools and national civil protection platforms, including early warnings and situational awareness tools, through guidance, common interfaces and technical support, in cooperation with Member States.
